prose.summary: The product meets the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate can be claimed. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED. Please refer to the checklist below.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, Doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The CEPA rate applies to Basic Customs Duty only, so other import charges such as IGST are still payable. The estimated saving is 10000.00 AED.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff subheading (CTSH) and a value addition (VA) of at least 45%. The final manufacture took place in the UAE and the work goes beyond the minimal operations that would not alone confer origin. All three non-originating inputs are classified outside subheading 761010, satisfying the CTSH requirement. The value added is 49.0% of the FOB price, which exceeds the 45% threshold.

notes.text: Electronic certificates are accepted and can be uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system under CBIC Instruction 28/2022. This information comes from secondary sources, not the official text.
UAE law requires keeping records for at least 3 years, but for CEPA claims you must keep them for 5 years.
The '+' in the rule CTSH + VA 45% is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual duty amounts will differ from the estimate. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

That electronic certificates are accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system comes from CBIC Instruction 28/2022, which Mansha has read only through secondary reports (LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The 40% value-added letter is a factory registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year recordkeeping minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
